title: Canonical catalog feed record
description: One record per line of an NDJSON feed. The source boundary of the pipeline: adapters emit these, the pipeline reads nothing else. No source system is named anywhere in this schema, by design.

code.description: A language-independent identifier from the source. Becomes part of a commercetools key, so it must be stable across exports.

localizedString.description: Locale tag to text. Tags must be IETF form (en-GB), not underscore form (en_GB).

decimalAmount.description: A monetary amount as a decimal string, e.g. "19.99". Never a JSON number: floats cannot represent decimal money exactly. Minor units are derived from the currency's fractionDigits at map time, and an amount with more decimal places than the currency allows is a hard error rather than a silent rounding.

url.description: Absolute, or relative as the source stores it. A relative URL needs media.baseUrl in the config to resolve against — validate refuses the pair rather than letting a host be guessed. This was `format: uri`, which made a relative path a schema violation and so forced adapter authors to invent a hostname to get the feed to validate.

attributeValue.description: A plain scalar, a localized string, or a set of either. The declared attributeDefinition decides how it is coerced; never infer the type from the value's shape alone. A set of localized strings is legal — the Import API has ltext-set — so array items may themselves be localized strings.

oneOf.description: A set. Element kind follows the declared type, not the value shape.

parent.description: Code of the parent category. Omit for a root. Forward references are allowed: order within the feed is not significant.

slug.description: Optional. When omitted the pipeline derives one from name and disambiguates it, because commercetools requires category slugs to be unique project-wide per locale.

orderHint.description: Optional sort position. commercetools expects a string in the open interval (0,1), NOT an integer. Supply a numeric source order in sourceOrder instead and let the pipeline encode it.

sourceOrder.description: A numeric sibling ordering from the source. The pipeline converts it to a valid orderHint preserving sequence.

assets.description: Media assets. Prefer these over `images` when the source has multiple renditions per shot.

attributeDefinition.description: Emit these when the source declares a type system. When absent, the pipeline infers definitions from observed values and forces an explicit review step — inference is a fallback, not the happy path.

name.description: commercetools attribute name. Must be language-independent.

type.description: The commercetools attribute type. Drive value coercion from this, never from a list of field names: a name allowlist fails silently on the next export.

level.description: product = invariant across variants, mapped to the SameForAll constraint. variant = may differ per variant.

axis.description: True when this attribute forms part of variant identity. Mapped to CombinationUnique. Only valid when level is variant.

values.description: Permitted values for enum and lenum types.

unit.description: Recorded as a decision and appended to the label. commercetools has no unit concept on attributes, so a bare number loses its unit otherwise.

searchable.description: Per-attribute searchability, when the source declares it. Absent falls back to productTypes.searchableByDefault. An axis is always searchable regardless.

slug.description: Optional; derived from name when omitted. Product slugs must be unique project-wide per locale.

productType.description: Groups products that share an attribute set. Omit to let the pipeline assign one; it will not invent a ProductType per product.

axes.description: Ordered list of attribute names that distinguish this product's variants. Every variant must supply a value for each. An empty or absent list means a single-variant product.

attributes.description: Product-level attribute values, invariant across variants.

externalId.description: The raw source identifier. Preserved separately from the key so downstream systems can still join on it.

selections.description: Which product selections carry this product. Authored on the product because one record per line is this contract's defining property; `plan` inverts it into ProductSelectionImport.assignments.

taxCategory.description: Code of a declared taxCategory. Held on the product, not the variant. Under the default Platform tax mode a cart takes its rate from this reference, so a product without one cannot be taxed at checkout; validate counts them.

sku.description: Unique across the whole feed. The permanent machine-readable identity of the sellable item.

product.description: Code of the owning product. Forward references are allowed.

axisValues.description: Language-independent CODE per axis, e.g. {"colour":"BLK"}. Display text belongs in axisLabels. This split is what stops a localized value becoming variant identity, which would make the same SKU key differently per language.

axisLabels.description: Display text per axis. Never used for identity or keying.

prices.description: Every price must be explicit. If the source inherits prices down a hierarchy, resolve the inheritance in the adapter: commercetools does not inherit prices between variants.

isMaster.description: Optional hint for which variant is the master. When no variant claims it, the pipeline picks deterministically by sorted SKU so the choice cannot drift between runs.

assets.description: Media assets. Prefer these over `images` when the source has multiple renditions per shot.

assetSource.description: One renderable file behind an asset. An asset may hold several, which is why a source with thumbnail/product/zoom renditions belongs in an asset rather than an image — an image carries exactly one URL.

uri.description: Absolute, or relative as the source stores it — resolved against media.baseUrl exactly as an image URL is.

key.description: Distinguishes renditions within one asset, e.g. `zoom`.

asset.description: A media asset on a variant or category. commercetools requires a key and at least one source; `name` is derived from `code` when absent and the derivation is recorded.

channel.description: A channel a price is scoped to. Declares a PREREQUISITE, not a resource this migration creates: the Import API has no channel resource, so the channel must already exist in the project and preflight verifies it. `code` is therefore the channel's actual key, used verbatim and never prefixed.

code.description: The channel's key in the project, verbatim.

roles.description: A price-scoped channel must include ProductDistribution; the API rejects a StandalonePrice referencing a channel without it.

customerGroup.description: A customer group a price is scoped to. A prerequisite like `channel`: the Import API cannot create one, so an unverified reference expires silently after 48 hours.

code.description: The customer group's key in the project, verbatim.

name.description: Required by the API; derived from the code when absent.

taxRate.description: One rate within a tax category. Identity within the category is (country, state); the API rejects a second rate for the same pair.

state.description: Case-sensitive; must match the casing carts use in shippingAddress.state. A rate with a state applies only to carts whose address carries the same state.

amount.description: A FRACTION, not a percentage: 0.2 for 20%. The API caps it at 1, and a source's `20` copied across would otherwise be a rate of 2000%.

includedInPrice.description: Whether prices are gross (true) or net (false) for this rate. No default on purpose: it decides how every price in the catalog is read, and getting it backwards shifts every price by the rate with nothing in the data to contradict it.

name.description: Required by the API and shown on orders as the tax portion's name. Derived from country and amount when absent, and recorded for review.

taxCategory.description: How a set of products is taxed, per country. A prerequisite like `channel`: the Import API has no tax-category resource, so load creates a missing one through the platform API and never modifies one that exists. `code` is the project's actual key, verbatim. Rates are used only when the category is created; an existing category keeps the project's rates and preflight reports any difference.

code.description: The tax category's key in the project, verbatim.

name.description: Required by the API and unique per project; derived from the code when absent.

rates.description: May be empty: correct when carts use External or ExternalAmount tax mode, wrong under Platform, so validate warns.

selectionMembership.description: One product's membership of one product selection. `includeSkus` and `excludeSkus` are mutually exclusive: the API accepts a variantSelection OR a variantExclusion, never both. With neither, every variant is included.

productSelection.description: A named subset of the catalog. Unlike channel and store this IS importable (Import API resource `product-selection`), so the key is prefixed like every other resource the migration creates. Inert until a store references it. `mode` is FIXED at creation and cannot be changed afterwards.

mode.description: Individual = allowlist, IndividualExclusion = denylist. Permanent. Defaults to Individual.

store.description: A shopping context. A PREREQUISITE like channel — the Import API has no store resource — so `code` is the project's actual key, verbatim. distributionChannels decide which prices apply (a price carries a channel; there is no store field on a price). productSelections decide which products exist; empty means all of them. supplyChannels is carried for fidelity but this pipeline imports no inventory. storefront URLs and custom fields are deliberately not supported.

code.description: The store's key in the project, verbatim.

distributionChannels.description: Codes of declared channels; each needs the ProductDistribution role.

supplyChannels.description: Codes of declared channels; each needs the InventorySupply role.

productSelections.description: At most 100. If every entry is inactive and at least one is Individual, the store exposes no products at all.

inventoryEntry.description: Stock for one SKU, optionally in one supply channel. A separate record rather than a field on `variant`, because stock is refreshed on a different cadence from the catalog and usually comes from a different source file: a feed can be regenerated for stock alone. Identity is (sku, supplyChannel) — the pair the API treats as unique — and the key is derived from it, so a re-run updates rather than duplicating.

sku.description: Must match a declared variant's sku. The Import API does not check this, so `validate` does: an entry for an unknown SKU imports successfully and is stock nobody can sell.

quantityOnStock.description: Overall stock, reserved included. Not availableQuantity, which the platform computes.

supplyChannel.description: Code of a declared channel carrying the InventorySupply role. Absent means project-wide stock for the SKU. A reference to a channel that does not exist leaves the operation unresolved for 48 hours, so the channel must be declared.

expectedDelivery.description: Date and time of the next restock, as an ISO-8601 instant.
